# Game model (7 levels)

## Layout (512x512)
- Top blue bar (y 8-16, x 8-496): action budget, 61 units; each game action turns 1 unit gray from the right.
- Board: interior x 112-400, y 72-328. Cells 32x32 → 9 columns (c0..c8) x 8 rows (r0..r7).
  - cell(r,c) origin: x = 112+32c, y = 72+32r. Center: (128+32c, 88+32r).
  - checkerboard: gray #262626 when (r+c) odd, black otherwise (cosmetic so far).
- Yellow ∩ piece = the mover (starts r1c4 in level 1). Yellow ∪ cup = goal (r6c4 in level 1); its interior is exactly one cell and it holds a nub matching the ∩'s notch.
- Control panel under board (y 336-384): 5 program slots. Slot i center x = 172,212,252,292,332 (spacing 40).
  - Each slot shows a "T": horizontal BAR (y 336-344, 24px wide) and vertical STEM (y 352-376, 8px wide, centered).
  - BLACK = instruction enabled, #CCCCCC gray = disabled.
  - Clicking the bar area (y≈336-350) toggles the bar; clicking the stem area (y≈352-376) toggles the stem. Independent toggles, 1 action each.
- Blue ball at (300,442) wired to the panel = RUN button.

## Execution
- Clicking RUN scans slots 1→5, one animation frame each (highlighted blue).
- Each slot with any black part performs one move that frame; all-gray slots are no-ops.
- BAR black ⇒ move DOWN 1 row. STEM black ⇒ move HORIZONTAL 1 column (direction not yet
  understood: observed +1, -1, and 0 in different situations).
- After the scan the piece RESETS to its start position if the goal wasn't reached.

## Strategy
Compute the needed net displacement from piece to cup and encode it in the ≤5 slots.
Prefer bar-only (pure down) steps while stem direction rules are unknown.

# Game model (7 levels)

## Layout (512x512)
- Top blue bar (y 8-16): action budget, 61 units; each game action greys 1 unit from the right.
- Board interior x 112-400, y 72-328. Cells 32x32 → 9 cols (c0..c8) x 8 rows (r0..r7).

- Yellow ∩ piece = mover. Yellow ∪ cup = goal; its interior is exactly one cell (with a nub

- Control panel under board: 5 program slots, centers x = 172, 212, 252, 292, 332.
  - Each slot has 2 independently toggled parts: BAR (horizontal, click y≈340) and
    STEM (vertical, click y≈364). BLACK = on, gray #CCCCCC = off. One click = one action.
- Blue ball at (300,442) = RUN.

## Instruction encoding (verified)
Per slot: BAR only → move LEFT 1. STEM only → move RIGHT 1. BAR+STEM (T) → move DOWN 1.
Neither → no-op (slot skipped). (UP not yet observed.)

## Execution
RUN scans slots 1→5 (one frame each, highlighted blue); each non-empty slot performs its
1-cell move. Falling off the board edge removes the piece. If the piece isn't in the cup at
the end of the scan, it resets to the start position and the level continues.

## Strategy
Read start cell and cup cell, compute needed sequence of ≤5 unit moves, set slots, RUN.
Cost = (#toggles needed) + 1 action.

# Game model (7 levels)

## Screen
- Top blue bar = action budget for the CURRENT level (~61 units, refills each level).
- A "machine" = a board (checkerboard) + a control panel of program slots + a RUN button
  (blue ball wired to it).
- Board cells are 32x32. Level 1 board: 9x8 at x112..400,y72..328. Level 2 right board: 7x7 at
  x264..488, y32..256 → cell(R,C) x=264+32C, y=32+32R.
- Yellow SOLID block with a notch = the mover. Yellow OUTLINE frame (with a nub matching the
  notch) = the goal cell. Goal = get the mover onto the frame's interior cell.
- Dimmed/gray machine(s) = DEMO/legend. Small boxes wired to a demo machine are buttons that
  run a demonstration program on it, revealing glyph→direction mappings.

## Program slots
- Each slot is a vertical column of stacked T-icons; each icon = BAR (horizontal, on top) +
  STEM (vertical, below). Level 1: 1 row per slot (5 slots). Level 2: 3 rows per slot (4 slots).
- Click a part to toggle it black (on) / gray (off). 1 click = 1 action.
  Click y-coords for a 3-row slot: barA 268, stemA 292, barB 316, stemB 340, barC 364, stemC 388.
- Number of slots = number of program steps = number of moves executed per RUN.

## Glyph → move (verified)
- {barA}            = LEFT 1
- {stemA}           = RIGHT 1
- {barA, stemA}     = DOWN 1
- {barA, stemC}     = UP 1        (from demo machine)
- {barB} alone, {stemA,barB} = no move (invalid glyphs)
- empty slot = no move

## RUN
Scans slots left→right, one frame each, executing its move. Piece leaving the board is lost.
If the mover isn't on the goal cell at the end, everything resets to the start position
(level is not failed; just retry).

## Strategy
Identify mover cell and goal cell, compute the move sequence (must fit exactly in the number
of slots), set each slot's parts, then RUN. Use demo buttons to learn unknown glyphs.

# Programmable-machine puzzle game (7 levels) — SOLVED

## Core structure
- Single ACTION6 (click) interface. Top blue bar = per-level action budget (refills each level).
- Right panel = the active MACHINE: board (32px cells) + program panel + blue RUN ball.
- Left dimmed panel = DEMO machine; small boxes below it are demo buttons. Clicking a box runs
  a demonstration on the demo machine AND displays the glyph that produces that effect.
  Box pictogram: yellow block = destination, white dots = path ⇒ movement is TOWARD the yellow.
  Other pictograms: big/small yellow square = GROW/SHRINK, diamond = ROTATE, colored square = recolor.

## Board objects
- Yellow SOLID block (with a notch) = mover. Yellow/colored OUTLINE frame with a matching nub
  = goal; win by ending on its interior cell(s) with matching size, color and notch orientation.
- Pink cells = walls (block movement). Yellow/black CHECKERED cells = checkpoints: if the mover
  ends a run on one, it stays there (no reset) — lets multi-run solutions exceed the slot count.
- Orange/red creature sprites on a row = beam emitters; the beam fills that whole row on some
  steps (observed: OFF on steps 1-2 of a run, ON from step 3). Entering the row while ON kills
  the mover (resets to last checkpoint).

## Program panel
- N slots side by side (5-6), each slot = a vertical column of 3 stacked T-icons:
  parts barA/stemA/barB/stemB/barC/stemC. Click a part to toggle black(on)/gray(off) — 1 action.
- Click y-coords: barA 268, stemA 292, barB 316, stemB 340, barC 364, stemC 388.
  Slot x-centers (6 slots): 276, 316, 356, 396, 436, 476.
- RUN executes slots left→right, one move/frame; empty slot = no-op; blocked move = no-op.
- The glyph→action mapping is RANDOMIZED PER LEVEL. Always learn it from the demo buttons
  (1 action each) before programming. Examples seen: {barA}=LEFT or UP, {stemA}=RIGHT,
  {barA,stemA}=DOWN or UP, {barA,stemC}=UP, {stemA,stemC}=LEFT, {stemB}=GROW,
  {barA,stemB}=SHRINK, {barA,barB}=ROTATE cw, all six parts = recolor.
- Size changes keep the piece's top-left corner. Rotation cycles the notch bottom→left→top→right.

## Winning method
1. Read the board: mover cell(s), goal cell(s), walls, checkpoints, hazards.
2. Plan a move sequence that fits the slot count; if too long, split into runs that each END on
   a checkpoint. Time hazard-row crossings to safe steps (step ≤2 of a run).
3. Click the needed demo boxes to learn glyphs, toggle the slots, press RUN.

[After action · message]
**Game complete: 7/7 levels, state = WIN.**

How the game worked, and how I solved it:

- **Mechanic discovered:** each level is a "machine" — a board plus a program panel of slots. Each slot is a column of bar/stem parts you toggle black; the pattern of black parts encodes one action (move, grow/shrink, rotate, recolor). Pressing the blue ball runs the program one slot per frame.
- **Key insight:** the glyph→action mapping is *randomized every level*, but the dimmed left machine is a demo/legend — clicking a demo button plays that action and simultaneously shows the exact glyph. That turned each level into: read board → plan sequence → learn only the glyphs I need → set slots → run.
- **Notable level solutions:**
  - L1–L3: straight/L-shaped paths, routing through a gap in the pink wall.
  - L4: SHRINK a 2×2 piece to squeeze through a 1-cell gap.
  - L5: DOWN×3 through a gap, then GROW, ROTATE (notch right→bottom) and recolor to purple to match the cup.
  - L6: the maze needed 12 steps with only 6 slots — solved by discovering checkered tiles are **checkpoints** (the piece persists there instead of resetting), splitting into two runs.
  - L7: a beam sweeps a whole row on a timer; I lost one probe run learning it fires from step 3, then used three checkpoint-to-checkpoint runs, crossing the beam row on step 2 when it is safe.
